Refused.description:
The command was not carried out. The body holds the refusal under `error`, with its code; a caller reads the code, and the status is worked out from it:

| Status | Codes |
|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_json` |
| 401 | `sign_in_refused`, `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `forbidden`, `reason_required` |
| 404 | `unknown_class`, `unknown_document`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_schema`, `unknown_app`, `unknown_blob`, `unknown_action`, `unknown_row`, `unknown_user`, `unknown_group`, `unknown_inlet`, `unknown_key`, `unknown_session`, `unknown_client`, `unknown_grant`, `unknown_invitation`, `unknown_passkey`, `unknown_command` |
| 409 | `key_reused`, `duplicate`, `terminal`, `stale_version`, `wrong_state`, `guard_false` |
| 413 | `blob_too_large`, `too_large` |
| 429 | `too_many_attempts` |
| 499 | `caller_left` |
| 500 | `storage`, `internal` |
| 503 | `closed`, `busy` |
| 504 | `timeout` |
| 422 | every other refusal |

info.description:
Every call that reads or changes a database is a command: a name and one JSON object, answered by one JSON object. A command is sent as `POST /v1/<command>` with its object as the body. A command that reads is a `POST` too, and the id of a document travels in the JSON and never in the address.

Who sends a request is never in the command. A database that keeps its own users is sent a key of a user, as `Authorization: Bearer fado_…`. A member that is `null` is a member left out, and a member a command does not have is refused.

This document is written from the engine's own table of the commands. The manual's chapter on the commands is written from the same table.
